question.problem: Given that $f(x)=5\cdot {7}^{x}$, the slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Applying the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\cdot {7}^{x}) \\  & =5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({7}^{x}) \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\cdot {7}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(5\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\cdot {7}^{x})|}_{x=0} \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\cdot {7}^{0} \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\cdot 1 \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(7).\end{aligned}
$$
